topic.title: Sine, Cosine, and Tangent
topic.summary: Angles in standard position, terminal rays, radian measure, and the sine, cosine, and tangent of an angle defined from a point on a circle centered at the origin.

questions.prompt: An angle θ is in standard position. Its terminal ray intersects a circle centered at the origin at the point (−3, 4). What is the value of sin θ?
questions.explanation: The point is √(9 + 16) = 5 units from the origin, so sin θ = (vertical displacement)/(distance) = 4/5.
choiceExplanations: −3/5 is cos θ, the horizontal displacement over the distance.
4 over the distance 5.
4 is the y-coordinate. It equals sin θ only when the circle has radius 1.
−4/3 is tan θ, the slope of the terminal ray.
questions.distinguisher: Divide by the radius unless the circle is a unit circle.

questions.prompt: Which of the following angles in standard position shares a terminal ray with an angle of π/3?
questions.explanation: 7π/3 = π/3 + 2π, one full revolution more, so the two angles share a terminal ray.
choiceExplanations: 4π/3 = π/3 + π is half a revolution more, which points the opposite way.
2π/3 is a different angle in Quadrant II.
−π/3 is the reflection of π/3 over the x-axis, a clockwise rotation into Quadrant IV.
7π/3 − π/3 = 2π, one revolution.
questions.distinguisher: Shared terminal rays differ by multiples of 2π, not by a sign change.

questions.prompt: An angle in standard position subtends an arc of length 10 centimeters on a circle of radius 4 centimeters centered at the origin. What is the radian measure of the angle?
questions.explanation: The radian measure is the ratio of arc length to radius: 10/4 = 2.5.
choiceExplanations: 0.4 = 4/10 is the radius over the arc length, the reciprocal of the radian measure.
40 multiplies the arc length and the radius.
Arc length divided by radius is 10/4 = 2.5.
10 is the arc length. It equals the radian measure only on a unit circle.
questions.distinguisher: Arc over radius, not radius over arc.

questions.prompt: The terminal ray of an angle θ in standard position passes through the point (2, −6). What is the value of tan θ?
questions.explanation: The tangent is the slope of the terminal ray: (−6 − 0)/(2 − 0) = −3.
choiceExplanations: The slope from (0, 0) to (2, −6) is −6/2 = −3.
−1/3 is horizontal change over vertical change, the reciprocal of the slope.
The ray goes down as it goes right, so its slope is negative.
−6 is the y-coordinate, not the slope.
questions.distinguisher: Tangent is y over x: rise over run.

questions.prompt: The terminal ray of an angle θ in standard position intersects the unit circle at the point (−0.8, −0.6). Which of the following is true?
questions.explanation: On the unit circle, sin θ is the y-coordinate, −0.6, and tan θ = y/x = (−0.6)/(−0.8) = 0.75.
choiceExplanations: −0.8 is the x-coordinate, which is cos θ.
Both coordinates are negative, so their ratio is positive.
cos θ is the x-coordinate, −0.8, and y/x is 0.75, not 4/3.
questions.distinguisher: On the unit circle P = (cos θ, sin θ): x first, then y.

questions.prompt: An angle of measure −π/2 is in standard position. At which point does its terminal ray intersect the unit circle?
questions.explanation: A negative measure is a clockwise rotation. A quarter turn clockwise from the positive x-axis lands on the negative y-axis, at (0, −1).
choiceExplanations: (0, 1) is a quarter turn counterclockwise, the angle π/2.
(−1, 0) is half a revolution, the angle π or −π.
A quarter revolution clockwise ends on the negative y-axis.
(1, 0) is no rotation at all.

questions.prompt: A bicycle wheel has a radius of 30 centimeters. The wheel turns through an angle of 2 radians. How far does a point on the rim of the wheel travel along the circle?
questions.explanation: The radian measure is arc length over radius, so the arc length is 30(2) = 60 cm.
choiceExplanations: 15 = 30/2 divides the radius by the angle; the arc length is the radius times the angle.
32 adds the radius and the angle measure.
188.5 ≈ 2π(30) is the distance for one full revolution, which is 2π radians, not 2 radians.
questions.distinguisher: Arc length is radius times radian measure.

questions.prompt: For which of the following angles θ in standard position is tan θ undefined?
questions.explanation: At θ = π/2 the terminal ray lies on the positive y-axis. A vertical ray has no slope, so tan θ is undefined.
choiceExplanations: At θ = π the ray lies on the negative x-axis, which is horizontal, so tan π = 0.
At θ = 0 the ray is horizontal, so tan 0 = 0.
At θ = π/4 the ray has slope 1.
The ray is vertical, so its slope does not exist.
questions.distinguisher: Undefined slope means a vertical ray, where cos θ = 0.

questions.prompt: The terminal ray of an angle θ in standard position passes through (4, 3), which lies on a circle of radius 5 centered at the origin. A student says sin θ = 3, because the sine of an angle is the y-coordinate of P. Which of the following is the best response?
choices: The student is correct, because 3 is the vertical displacement of P from the x-axis.
The student is incorrect, because the y-coordinate equals the sine only on a unit circle; here sin θ = 3/5.
The student is incorrect, because sin θ = 4/5, the x-coordinate over the radius.
The student is incorrect, because sin θ = 3/4, the slope of the terminal ray.
questions.explanation: The sine is the vertical displacement divided by the distance from the origin, 3/5. Only when that distance is 1 does the sine equal the y-coordinate itself.
choiceExplanations: The vertical displacement must be divided by the distance from the origin, 5.
Divide the vertical displacement 3 by the radius 5.
4/5 uses the horizontal displacement, which gives cos θ.
3/4 is the slope, which is tan θ.
questions.distinguisher: Sine uses the vertical displacement; cosine uses the horizontal one.

questions.prompt: For an angle θ in standard position, sin θ < 0 and tan θ > 0. In which quadrant does the terminal ray of θ lie?
questions.explanation: sin θ < 0 puts P below the x-axis. tan θ = y/x > 0 then needs x < 0 as well, so the ray is in Quadrant III.
choiceExplanations: In Quadrant I, sin θ > 0.
In Quadrant II, sin θ > 0 and tan θ < 0.
y < 0 and x < 0 make y/x positive.
In Quadrant IV, sin θ < 0, but x > 0 makes tan θ < 0.
questions.distinguisher: A positive tangent needs x and y with the same sign.
